main_text.l: nicia urbs, ut Tyrus, celeberrima quondam metropolis, & Tyro ducentis tantum stadijs distans. Semen Nili in aquis multis, periphrasticēs pro frugibus Aegyptijs, quae fouentur & proueniunt inundatione aquarum Nili, sicut ipse propheta suis uerbis interpretatur. Subindicat autem, ex omnibus Aegypti oris merces Tyrum conuehi solitas. Nonnulli per Insulam intelligunt Cyprum, prophetamq; uelle, ut haec quoq; lugeat, propterea quod mercatores, imprimis Sidonij, no amplius Tyrum, sed potius in Cyprum nauigare cogentur. Sed enim Cyprus hic non dolendi, at potius laetandi haberet materiam. Quare meo iudicio non satis apte ad Cyprum uerba fieri dixerint.

Erubesce Zidon, quia dixit.) Secunda amplificatio, a succedente maxima rerum penuria. Per apostrophen dirigit orationem ad Sidonem, eamque ulterius pudore suffundi propter Tyrum, ob quam antea solita erat maximopere gloriari. Deinde per prosopopoeiam introducit ipsam Tyrum (quasi cita periphrasi ob celebritatem ac potentiam uocat Mare & Fortitudinem maris) conquerentem, quod nullum amplius commodum mercatoribus seu uicinis ciuitatibus afferre queat. Lucrum & commodum ex mercibus per allegoriam se habent instar foetus ac sobolis. Vel certe deplorat Tyrus, quod non amplius ut olim possit colonias alio deducere, ciuitates ac uiculos nouos condere. Nam referente etiam Plinio lib. 5. cap. 19. Tyrus olim partu clara

page.notes: Catchword "clara" at foot right; the text continues on the next page. Page number and running head read from the printed head. The first paragraph begins mid-sentence from the previous page and is marked cont="true". The page is set in roman type with a few italic runs, rendered in <i>. Possible doubtful readings: "Erubesce" (final letter may be a Cyrillic-like look-alike, copied as Latin e), "ulterius" in the line "eamque ulterius pudore" is read as printed "ult pudore" with the abbreviation ult; this is uncertain and should be checked. "commodum" appears in both "Lucrum & commodum" and "mercatoribus" lines as printed. The Greek phrase "periphrasticēs" is printed as "periphrasticės" and is uncertain.
